hypotheses.note: (flatCausality 2 N).IsCauchySurface Sigma; topological, as everywhere in btz

hypotheses.paper: Sigma cap S lies in the shaft of S
hypotheses.note: as for lem:add_BTZ_param (DEC-116 (c)): Sigma cap S in {tau > v + R'/2}

hypotheses.paper: tau_Sigma smooth on D*_R, values in R_+^*
hypotheses.note: continuous on the punctured closed disc {0 < |z| <= R'}, values > v + R'/2: DEC-125 (c)'s reading of the twin lem:add_BTZ_param (Sigma is a topological Cauchy surface; smoothness is not claimed, for the same reason as there; no counterexample formalized for the blunt case)

hypotheses.paper: (implicit in 'essentially the same' proof) the regular null rays of S0 are inextensible in M
hypotheses.note: flat_vertical_noLimit, flat_infall_noLimit; the core takes them as hypotheses hvert, hfall

sorries.obstruction: a vertical null ray t -> psi(t, z), z != 0, of a blunt spear chart into a flat N has no future endpoint. Needs rigidity at a REGULAR limit point q: kappa o psi, kappa the Minkowski chart at q, equals one isometry times the sector chart on the connected tube around the ray (e0_eqOn_of_eqOn_open needs a global element of e0Groupoid built from sectorChartBTZ, and the library has no lemma that sectorChartBTZ lies in BTZE0's maximal a.e. atlas); then the developed ray (2t + r theta^2 - r, r, -r theta) is unbounded. E0Spear.axis_noLimit's route (btzE0_localUnique_core) works only at a BTZ limit point.

an in-falling null ray s -> psi(a + s/2, s u), s -> 0+, a > v, has no past endpoint in a flat N. The developed ray CONVERGES (to the developed axis point (2a,0,0)), so unboundedness gives nothing: one must show that psi extends, through the Minkowski chart at the limit point, to a full punctured neighbourhood of the axis point, and then that the two sector charts around the axis (which differ by the parabolic holonomy hol(2 pi) on one overlap component, kb/0107, chartMap_eq_hol_smul) cannot both be one isometry times the chart at q. Not formalized.

findings: BTZ_1.tex:721 (« the proof of Lemma lem:blunt_spear_neighborhood is essentially the same ») — it is not: the proof of lem:add_BTZ_param (l.722–741) starts from the vertex p in I^-(Sigma) (« there exists U a neighborhood of w on which inf(tau o Phi(U cap Sigma)) > tau o Phi(p) ») and from the BTZ ray through p, neither of which exists in M* (the vertex is not a point of M*, and the lemma has no hypothesis placing anything below Sigma). A proof is in GX.E0BluntSpear.lem_blunt_spear_of_inextensible: compare in E0 (le_of_small_rad: a point of radius r1 <= r2/2 is below every point of radius r2 whose f-level is 4 pi^2 r1 higher) with ONE point of Sigma found on a far in-falling null ray or above it (binfall_meets / bvertical_meets); it needs that the vertical and in-falling regular null rays of S0 are inextensible in M, which the paper does not state and which is a rigidity/holonomy fact (two tagged sorrys).

BTZ_1.tex:1601–1604 (theo:BTZ_Cauchy-completness, Step 1): the lemma is applied to Sigma_0, a Cauchy surface of M_0, with S the spear of M_2 given by lem:tube; reg(S) is a blunt spear of M_2^* but is shown to lie in M_0 only afterwards (l.1604, « we deduce that N subset M_0 »), so at l.1601 the lemma's hypothesis « a blunt spear neighborhood in M » (M = M_0) is not yet available. Not formalized; recorded as a possible ordering gap for the author.

BTZ_1.tex:698: « phi : S -> Reg(E_0) » versus « phi_0 : S_0 -> E_0 »; and l.699 « graph of a smooth function tau_Sigma : D_R^* -> R_+^* » with R the radius of S (not of S_0), which the statement leaves implicit; read so.
questions: « inf(phi(S)) = inf(phi(S0)) » (l.698) is not defined; read as the infimum for the causal order of E0 (the vertex), formalized as equality of the sets of lower bounds (lowerBounds_bspear_iff). The other natural reading, the infimum of the tau-coordinate, is also preserved (it is v for every radius), but only the causal reading is in the Lean statement.
« Sigma cap S lie in the shaft of S » read as {tau > v + R'/2}, the reading DEC-116 (c) ruled for lem:add_BTZ_param.
Smoothness of tau_Sigma read as continuity (DEC-125 (c), ruled for the twin lemma, not for this one).

kb_proposals: E0 comparison without angles: GX.E0BluntSpear.le_of_small_rad — rad x <= rad y / 2 and 4 pi^2 rad x <= fcoord y - fcoord x give Le x y (from le_iff_closed, |arg - arg| <= 2 pi).
CE (FlatE0 N) = Causal.Flat.flatCausality 2 N as Causality structures (GX.E0BluntSpear.ce_flatE0_eq, Causality.ext + flatE0_rel_iff): rewrite GH and Cauchy hypotheses across with rw [<- h] at hyp.

A blunt spear avoids the axis along causal relations (rad is monotone, J^+ of a regular point of E0 misses the axis): GX.E0BluntSpear.le_of_le_top_of_mem_bspear is the blunt le_of_le_top_of_mem_spear.

Inextensibility of regular null rays in a flat N (vertical: unbounded development; in-falling: needs the parabolic holonomy across two sector charts) is open; the missing brick is sectorChartBTZ in BTZE0's maximal a.e. atlas.
